For the typical Laparoscopic Appendectomy, the total cost of the procedure is $33,000 with a doctor fee of $1,600, which I assume is paid to the surgeon. With that said the other $33,000 is used to cover all the other expenses. A typical appendectomy patient will stay in the hospital for 2-3 days following surgery. Prices can definitely add up during this time, since wages are paid to nurses/doctors for not just the surgery, but also for the entire 48-72 hours of hospital stay. The average salary for a nurse is $32.00 and the average internal medicine doctor is probably pulling in around $100 an hour... but he is also covering multiple patients, same with the nurse. You can see why the price exactly is hard to calculate, with so many factors. Plus the hospital system wants to make a hefty profit. And the drug companies, and the device companies.

Not just that, but the docs/hospital charge more for people who can pay to subsidize for all the patients who don't. This is due to the fact that the hospital can't turn anyone away who desperately needs their help, even if they can't pay.
